narr: Training showers and thunderstorms developed along a slow moving frontal boundary stretching from Connecticut to Southwest Maine on the evening of the 11th. The anomalously moist airmass caused moderate to heavy widespread rain of 1 to 3 inches. A localized axis of heavy rainfall between 4 to 6 inches extended from central Massachusetts across the Stateline and into Nashua, New Hampshire. Flash flooding developed over Nashua, Hollis, and Hudson with numerous water rescues and flooded basements.
ev: Unofficial rain gage stations reported rainfall amounts between 2 to 6 inches between Hollis, Nashua, and Hudson. Nashua Fire Department responded to multiple calls of people trapped in their cars. There were about a dozen reports of flooded basements, according to Nashua Emergency Management. Both Dow Road and Twiss Lane remained closed for a long duration due to damage from floodwaters. A parking area to an apartment complex off Northeastern Boulevard had up to 4 feet of standing water, damaging dozens of cars.
NH-130, also known as Proctor Road, was closed due to flood waters between Rocky Pond Rd and Kerk Drive. Floods damaged Proctor Hill Road from Rocky Pond Rd in Hollis to the Brookline town line.

Water several feet deep in June street with reports upwards of 3-4FT. Flooding was caused by heavy rainfall on the evening of the 11th. Unofficial weather station in the Hudson area recorded over 5 inches of rain between 5 and 8 PM.
lsr: Road impassable with multiple cars stuck in water.
